commit_scope: GET /api/sensings?kind= answered [] in production because the kind filter and the ordering read a nested `properties` key the graph service never fills (it flattens properties onto the node, as _is_sensing and _node_to_sensing already read); they now read the flattened node with the nested key as fallback.
evidence_refs: Observed live 2026-10-20 00:11 WITA on revision 79cd36862: GET /api/sensings?limit=2 → [sensing-20261019T154519-509b61 skin, sensing-20260519T155757-9b5db2 skin]; GET /api/sensings?kind=skin&limit=2 → []. The concept page's WorldSignals component asks exactly ?kind=skin&limit=10.

Root cause in api/app/routers/sensings.py: list_sensings filtered on (n.get('properties') or {}).get('sensing_kind') and sorted on properties.observed_at, while _is_sensing and _node_to_sensing read the flattened node (comment in the file: graph_service flattens properties onto the top level). The filter could never match.
Fix: _node_property reads the flattened key first and the nested key as fallback; the filter, the sensing test and the ordering use it (ordering falls back to created_at).

tests/test_source_artifact_sensing_graph.py: new test_list_sensings_filters_kind_on_the_flattened_node (flattened and nested nodes, kind filter, ordering); file: 3 passed, pytest exit code read directly.
